transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hello. Lately I can’t seem to focus at work—my mind keeps drifting back to everything that could go wrong with my job. It's just making it really hard to get through my day-to-day tasks, and I felt like I needed to talk to someone about it.
How long have you been feeling this way, and do you worry about several different areas of your life most days, or mainly just about work?

This has been going on steadily for about nine months, ever since they announced a reorganization at the clinic where I work. While the worries are heavily focused on my job—like making mistakes or failing if my role changes—they've definitely spilled over into other areas, like worrying about paying rent and not even being able to enjoy my hobbies or free time because my mind is constantly racing.
When you’re feeling worried, do you also get physical symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, fatigue, trouble sleeping, irritability, or feeling on edge?

Yes, absolutely. My body feels constantly revved up and tense, especially my shoulders, and I can't seem to relax even when I'm at home. My sleep has also been terrible; I lie awake for hours replaying the day and wake up multiple times during the night worrying.
Do you ever have sudden episodes of intense fear or panic that peak within minutes, with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest tightness, or feeling like you might lose control?

No, I don't experience those sudden, intense episodes of panic or physical symptoms like a racing heart or trouble breathing. Instead, it feels more like a constant, lingering state of tension and worry that stays with me all day long.
How much has this worry and tension affected your ability to work, take care of daily responsibilities, or enjoy your life?

It has really taken a toll on my life. At work, my manager has had to point out scheduling mistakes more often and I'm falling behind on emails. I've also had to pull back from my art workshops, volunteering, and photography because I feel too overwhelmed to keep up with them.
Have you also been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy most days?

I wouldn't say I feel hopeless, but I've definitely stopped doing the things I normally love, like my art workshops, photography, and volunteering. I just feel too overwhelmed, tense, and constantly distracted by my worries to actually keep up with them or enjoy them anymore.
In the past few months, have you often felt depressed, hopeless, or lost interest/pleasure in things most days?

No, I wouldn't say I feel depressed or hopeless, and I haven't actually lost interest in my hobbies. It's just that I feel so overwhelmed, anxious, and physically exhausted that I don't have the energy to keep up with my art workshops or volunteering right now.
Did these symptoms start within a few months of the clinic reorganization, and if the work situation had not changed, do you think they would have happened or continued?

Yes, they started right around nine months ago when the reorganization was first announced. I really don't think I would be experiencing all this worry and tension if things had just stayed stable at work, as the uncertainty of the changes is what triggered everything.
Have your symptoms been present for more than 6 months after the stressor started, or do they usually improve once you feel the work situation is more settled?

Yes, they've been going on steadily for about nine months now, so it has definitely been longer than six months. They haven't really improved or settled down at all, mostly because the situation at work is still unresolved and the uncertainty is ongoing.
Did these worries and tension start only after the work reorganization, and would you say they are out of proportion to what’s happening or persist even when you’re away from work?

Yes, they started right after the reorganization was announced and they definitely persist when I'm away from work, like when I'm trying to watch a show or relax on the couch. The worries also feel completely out of proportion, because something as small as a typo in an email makes me spiral into worrying that I'll lose my job and won't be able to pay rent.
Did the anxiety begin only after the work reorganization, and has it stayed tied to that stressor without happening before in the same way?

Yes, it only started after the reorganization was announced. I've had normal stress in the past, but this constant, uncontrollable worry and physical tension is completely new and has remained steady ever since this transition began.
Before the clinic reorganization, had you ever had a similar pattern of constant worry and physical tension for months at a time, or is this the first time you've experienced anything like this?
I don't recall ever experiencing this level of constant worry and physical tension before. This definitely feels like the first time it has ever been this bad.
Before this work reorganization, had you ever had a similar pattern of constant worry and physical tension for months at a time, or is this the first time you've experienced anything like this?

No, I've never experienced anything like this before the reorganization. I've had normal, everyday stress in the past, but never this kind of constant, overwhelming worry and physical tension. This is definitely the first time it has ever been like this.
Since the clinic reorganization started, have you had any nightmares, flashbacks, or strong avoidance of reminders of it, like refusing to think or talk about work changes?

No, I haven't had any nightmares or flashbacks, and I don't try to avoid thinking about it. It's actually the opposite—I can't seem to stop thinking about it, and my mind just constantly loops back to the work changes and what could go wrong.
Have your symptoms improved at all when the work situation feels more stable, or do the worry and tension stay just as strong even when there are no new changes at work?

No, they haven't improved at all; the worry and tension have remained completely steady over the last nine months. Even when there are no new changes or when I try to distract myself, that loop of worry keeps running in my head. My body just stays too tense to relax, no matter what.

Have you had any major life stressor besides the work reorganization that could explain these symptoms, or is the anxiety mainly tied to that one situation? Also, has the worry been present most days for at least 6 months even when there are no new work changes?

No, there haven't been any other major life stressors; the anxiety is really just tied to the work reorganization and the uncertainty about my role and income, on top of my tendency to over-commit myself. These worries have definitely been present almost every single day for the entire nine months since it all started. Even on days when nothing new is happening at the clinic, the constant looping thoughts and tension don't let up.
Did the anxiety and tension begin only after the work reorganization, and have they stayed tied to that stressor without ever occurring in the same way before?

Yes, it definitely started about nine months ago when the reorganization was first announced. While I've had normal day-to-day worries in the past, I've never experienced this kind of constant, looping worry and physical tension before this transition. It has been going on steadily ever since.
Have your symptoms clearly improved or gone away once the work situation became more stable, or do the worry and tension continue even when the stressor is no longer present?

The work situation hasn't actually settled down or become stable yet, as the uncertainty surrounding the reorganization is still very much ongoing. Because of that, the worry and tension have been constant and steady for the past nine months without any relief.

Have you ever had a similar period of constant worry and tension before this work reorganization, or is this the first time it has happened? Also, if the work situation were to fully settle, do you think your symptoms would go away within a few months?

I'm not really sure if I've ever experienced anything quite this intense before. Also, I haven't really thought about whether my symptoms would completely go away if the work situation finally settled.
If the work situation were to fully settle down, do you think your worry and tension would fade within a few months, or would they likely keep going even after the stress is over?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. While I would hope things would get better if work finally settled down, the worry and tension feel so constant and hard to turn off right now. It's just really difficult to imagine them completely disappearing.
If the work reorganization were fully resolved, do you think your anxiety and tension would fade within a few months, or would they keep going even after the stress is over?

I honestly don't know. The worry is so constant and overwhelming right now that I can't even picture what it would feel like for things to be normal again. I would hope it would go away, but it's just really hard to imagine that far ahead right now.
If the work reorganization were fully resolved, do you think your worry and tension would start to fade within a few months, or would they likely keep going even after the stress is over?

I'm really not sure. While I would hope that resolving the reorganization would help, this worrying loop feels so constant and automatic now. I just don't know if I'd be able to switch it off even if everything at the clinic got sorted out.
If the work reorganization were fully resolved, do you think your worry and tension would start to fade within a few months, or would they likely keep going even after the stress is over?

I'm really not sure and I haven't really thought about it. Right now, I'm so caught up in the middle of this ongoing reorganization and the daily worry that it's just really hard to imagine what things would feel like if it were completely resolved.
If the work reorganization were fully resolved, do you think your worry and tension would start to fade within a few months, or would they likely keep going even after the stress is over?

I'm really not sure because I haven't thought about whether the worry would actually stop. Since the situation is still so unsettled right now, it's just hard to predict how I would feel if everything were resolved.
If the work reorganization were fully resolved, do you think your worry and tension would start to fade within a few months, or would they likely keep going even after the stress is over?

To be honest, I'm just not sure how I would feel if the reorganization were finally resolved. Because this loop of worry feels so constant and overwhelming right now, it's really hard to imagine it just stopping, but I honestly don't know.
Have your anxiety and tension ever lasted for at least 6 months after a stressful situation ended, or do they usually improve once the stressor is gone?

I'm really not sure about that. Since the reorganization at the clinic is still ongoing, I haven't had a chance to see if my anxiety would actually go away after the stressor ends. Plus, I've never experienced this kind of worry before, so I don't have any past experiences to compare it to.
If the clinic reorganization were fully resolved, do you think your worry and tension would go away within a few months, or would they likely keep going even after the stress is over?
I honestly can't say for sure. I would certainly hope they'd fade, but the loop of worrying feels so constant and automatic now that it's really hard to imagine it just stopping.
If the clinic reorganization were fully resolved, do you think your worry and tension would fade within a few months, or would they likely keep going even after the stress is over?

I would hope that the anxiety and tension would go away once the reorganization is resolved. However, because my mind is currently in such a constant loop of worrying, I honestly aren't sure if I'd just find new things to stress about.
If the clinic reorganization were fully resolved, do you think your anxiety and tension would go away within a few months, or would they likely keep going even after the stress is over?
I'm really not sure because I've never dealt with this kind of anxiety before. It is hard to know if it would just fade away or if the worrying has just become my new normal.
If the clinic reorganization were fully resolved, do you think your worry and tension would go away within a few months, or would they likely keep going even after the stress is over?

I'm really not sure. While I hope things would go back to normal once the reorganization is resolved, I feel so stuck in this constant loop of worry and tension right now that it's hard to imagine it just turning off.
